text: The summary query works, but right now it's just a query someone has to remember to paste in and re-run. This lesson wraps it in a view, and finishes the one grant that's been waiting since last lesson.

Create or replace view, named VW underscore daily underscore ticket underscore summary, defined as exactly the summary query from lesson five. A view has no stored data of its own — every time something reads it, it re-runs that underlying query against whatever's currently in the raw tickets table.

That's why a view, and not a table that gets refreshed on some schedule, is the right call here. A table needs its own refresh logic to stay current. A view just stays current automatically, because it never stops re-running its own query. For a project this size, that's strictly simpler, and simpler wins when nothing demands otherwise.

Now that the view exists, we can finish the grant chain from last lesson: grant select on this view, to the support analyst role. That's the one piece Lesson 6 couldn't grant yet, because the object didn't exist until right now.

The real test isn't whether that GRANT statement ran without an error — it's switching into the role itself and actually querying. Use role, support analyst. Use warehouse. Select from the view. If that returns rows, the chain is complete end to end: warehouse, database, schema, and now the view itself.

The view exists, the role can read it, and it's always current. Next lesson, we connect the one tool that's been the whole point of this project from the start: Power BI, pointed directly at this view.
